summary: Iteration 2 review — 6 new features (Resend email, Google OAuth, Stripe registration fee, KZ license gate, CSV bid export, EN/RU/KK i18n). Backend pytest suite extended from 30 → 44 tests, ALL 44 PASSED. Frontend Playwright verified: landing/login/register lang switcher (KK & RU translations render), Google buttons present and redirect to auth.emergentagent.com, vendor fee banner + Pay CTA, /vendor/payment amount + Stripe button, vendor profile fee-banner + KZ license block (6 buttons on step 4 when country=KZ), buyer /buyer/create KZ block with 6 license buttons. No blocking issues.

minor.issue: Endpoint is public (no auth dependency) — any user knowing a session_id can read status/payment_status. Low risk since session_ids are opaque but consider requiring vendor auth.
handle_webhook raises => endpoint returns 400 for any failure including replay/dup; Stripe may retry indefinitely. Consider idempotent 200 on already-processed events.

Gate only triggers when ALL 6 declarations are True. Sending decl_fee=False bypasses the gate entirely and lets vendor save profile without paying. Consider always requiring fee_paid regardless of decl toggle, or forcing decl_fee=True on submit.

origin_url is taken from request body — a malicious vendor could pass any URL and cause success_url to redirect to attacker-controlled domain after payment. Consider whitelisting against FRONTEND_URL.

issues: Still uses native browser datetime-local picker (same as iter1 note) — inconsistent with shadcn design system.
'Next step' remains unconditional; users can skip required fields and only see failure on final submit.

action_items: (Optional / security) Require vendor auth on GET /api/payments/status/{session_id}, or at minimum enforce user_id match.
(Optional / security) Whitelist origin_url in POST /api/payments/checkout against FRONTEND_URL to prevent open-redirect via success/cancel URLs.
(Optional / correctness) Make Stripe webhook idempotent — return 200 on already-paid transactions instead of raising 400.
(Optional / UX) Force decl_fee logically or always require fee_paid regardless of decl toggle so vendors can't save profile bypass by unchecking a declaration.
(Carry-over from iter1) Replace native datetime input with shadcn DatePicker on CreateTender.
(Carry-over from iter1) Per-step validation on VendorProfile 'Next step'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 902 lines — routers/models split is overdue. Consider splitting payments, auth (google+password), reference data, and email helper into modules.
STRIPE_API_KEY default 'sk_test_emergent' hardcoded in 3 places — extract to a module-level constant or single wrapper.
list_bids buyer branch when mine=false still computes my_tender_ids list even when tender_id is given (dead branch preserved from iter1).

Google callback: when the user is new and role is None, endpoint returns {needs_role: true} but does NOT set any cookie or short-lived token — the second call must resubmit the same session_id and pray it's still valid on Emergent's side. Consider storing a temporary bridge token.
Payment webhook returns 400 on Exception — Stripe will retry forever on transient DB errors. Return 200 for anything that's not a signature failure and log the internal error.

csv_export writes proposal after .replace('\n', ' ') but does not strip carriage returns or handle embedded quotes explicitly (csv.writer does escape quotes, so OK). No CSV-injection guard for values starting with =, +, -, @ — a malicious vendor could inject formulas. Consider prefixing suspicious cells with '.
seed_admin_and_demo silently reseeds only admin password; buyer/vendor passwords never rotate.
